atomicity.reason: Two aspects: the greater-than-250 mV median-deviation classification, and the rule that an invalid measurement is not used to evaluate a cell-protection limit. The second is closely related, but it is a separate usage obligation - and it is already carried normatively by the 'valid measurement' wording in the limit requirements, while here it is stated in the indicative rather than as a shall.
atomicity.suggestion: Keep the classification as the single shall-clause and drop the exclusion sentence (already implied by the limit requirements) or promote it to its own requirement.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: it states the compared quantities, the threshold and the consequence of the invalid mark.

feasibility.reason: Implementable as written, but it works against REQ_CELL_VOLTAGE_LIMITS: a cell collapsing below 2.50 V while its module median sits near 3.7 V deviates by roughly 1200 mV, is classified invalid, and is then excluded from limit evaluation - so the single-cell undervoltage case the protection exists for is suppressed. The two requirements are only formally consistent because the limit requirement is scoped to 'valid' measurements.
feasibility.suggestion: Bound the check so it cannot suppress protection: apply it only to readings inside the safe window, require corroboration (a second sensor or a redundant path) before discarding an out-of-range reading, or treat a persistent outlier as a fault in its own right rather than as a discardable measurement.

parent_fit.reason: The parent story's obligation is that the pack disconnects when a cell leaves its safe window; this requirement constrains how measurements are qualified rather than delivering any part of that capability, and its exclusion rule can work against the parent's promise that no single cell is driven into a runaway condition.
parent_fit.suggestion: Trace it to the obligation it really serves (not disconnecting the pack on a single failed sensor), and state the diagnostic reaction to a persistently invalid sensor so the parent's safety promise is not silently weakened.

unambiguity.reason: One reading - the absolute deviation of a cell voltage from the median of its own module's cell voltages.

verifiability.reason: 250 mV, the module median and the absolute difference are concrete, and the exclusion clause supplies a black-box test: an implausible out-of-range reading must not open the contactors.

summary: LOUD FLAG: the plausibility rule as written can mask the very fault the voltage-limit requirement exists to catch. A genuinely collapsed cell deviates from its module median by far more than 250 mV, is therefore marked invalid, and is then excluded from limit evaluation - so no contactor-open command is issued.
